mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-01.prompt: If $N$ is a 3-digit integer, and given that the result of reversing the digits of $N$ is the number $M$, what is the maximum value of $N-M$? [Note: Integers written with 1 or more leading zeros can also be written with every leading zero removed.]

mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-02.prompt: If $a$ and $b$ are integers whose product is 5, what is the least possible value of $a^b$?

mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-03.prompt: Al's biplane can fly two different types of square advertising signs. Both signs have integer side-lengths. Their areas are $n+1$ and $2n+1$. What is the least positive integer $n$ for which each sign's area is the square of an integer?

mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-04.prompt: In a group of 100, each a Borg or a Corg, every Borg has 2 Corg friends and no Corg has more than 1 Borg friend. If exactly 13 Corgs have no Borg friends, then how many Corgs are in the group?

mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-05.prompt: If $2019!$ is the product of the first 2019 positive integers, for which positive integer $k$ is $x = 2019!$ the only value of $x > 0$ that satisfies $$\frac{1}{\log_4 x} + \frac{1}{\log_9 x} + \frac{1}{\log_{16} x} + \cdots + \frac{1}{\log_{(2019^2)} x} = k?$$

mathleague-2018-19-hs-c5-06.prompt: Midpoints of two sides of a square are vertices of the shaded triangle shown. Drawing the diagonal of the square pictured splits this triangle into two parts, one of which is a trapezoid. If the area of the square is 192, what is the area of the trapezoid?
